title: Transient OOM bloom: KV cache tombstone compaction + runtime page-throttle stitch
creator: Ava Chen
description: Multiple customers (healthcare and fintech pilots) reported intermittent GPU OOM cascades across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Root cause analysis indicates a long-lived buildup of KV cache tombstone metadata that accelerates slab fragmentation under mixed short/long sequence workloads. This combined with a bursty page allocation pattern produced transient page-surge events that exhaust device memory and cascade into neighboring sessions. The fix combines a lightweight tombstone compaction pass (bloom-assisted) with a runtime page-throttle and a compact-on-idle slab stitcher to avoid synchronous pauses.
repro_steps: 1) Start a multi-tenant workload with 60% short-chat and 40% long-streaming sequences (sequence length mix: 16/2048).
2) Enable prefix KV caching and reproduce steady-state for 36+ hours with normal traffic shaping (1-2% tail bursts).
3) Inject a tenant that performs frequent ephemeral sessions that create and delete many small keys (pattern: create/delete/renew every 2-10s).
4) Observe slab fragmentation growth and GPU allocation failures in telemetry (OOM count increases; page-surge spikes).
observed_metrics: GPU_OOM_rate: spike from 0.0 to 2.3 / hour during incident windows
KV_tombstone_ratio: rose from 0.8% to 18% in affected arenas
mitigations_applied: Hotpatch: introduced a soft throttle that limits concurrent page-reserve requests per tenant (deployed to Hosted canary within 30m).
Operational: forced session affinity to unaffected pools for high-priority customers while patch is validated.
Customer comms: provided targeted runbooks and temporary quota increases to affected customers as stopgap.

decisions_and_tradeoffs: 1) Chose incremental bloom-assisted compaction over full-index rebuild to avoid expensive downtime. Tradeoff: small false-positive compaction passes accepted to keep latency bounded.

2) Implemented a conservative page-throttle (requests/sec cap) to provide graceful backpressure rather than immediate eviction. Tradeoff: temporary increase in tail latency for heavy tenants during bursts.

3) Deferred an aggressive eager slab defragmenter (would require memory spikes) in favor of a compact-on-idle stitcher that runs when headroom is available. Tradeoff: fragmentation reduced over hours instead of minutes.
